0.why: Front view over the fence: ears spread either side, both eyes, the long face down to the muzzle at the bottom edge.

4.why: Still facing us; the head has drifted a little right with the camera. Holding the front view.

8.why: End of the front hold; the face starts to widen on its right side, the first sign of the turn.

10.why: Turn begins: muzzle starts toward the right, the right ear swings back.

12.why: Three-quarter view: the far eye slides toward the nose line, the muzzle points down-right.

14.why: More than half turned: the face outline becomes the profile, the far ear is tucked behind the near one.

16.why: Almost in profile; the head starts to reach forward and down.

19.why: Full profile at the forward extreme: the head stretches out over the rail, muzzle furthest right.

20.why: Holding the forward reach for a moment before the head drops.

24.why: Profile, the head starts to tip down: the muzzle drops while the camera tilts after it.

28.why: Head tipping down past the rails toward the hay, nose now under the eye.

30.why: Breakdown: the head hangs straight down, muzzle just above the hay.

32.why: THE LINE: the muzzle reaches the hay; the head, turned into profile and stretched out over the rail, now hangs nearly straight down from the poll.

34.why: Settle after the contact: the muzzle pushes into the pile and the head starts to swing left.

36.why: Muzzle pushed into the hay pile and swung left, the camera still tilting down.

38.why: Eating: the muzzle down in the pile, lowest point of the bite.

40.why: Eating: the head lifts a little with a mouthful.

42.why: Eating: the muzzle drops back into the hay further right.

44.why: Settle: nose in the hay, head down, chewing.
